headings: Contracts with Supply Partners and Customers
paragraphs: Digital Turbine, Inc., through its subsidiaries (collectively "Digital Turbine," the "Company," "we," or "us"), is a leading independent mobile growth platform that levels up the landscape for advertisers, publishers, carriers, and device original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs"). The Company offers end-to-end products and solutions leveraging proprietary technology to all participants in the mobile application ecosystem, enabling brand discovery and advertising, user acquisition and engagement, and operational efficiency for advertisers. In addition, our products and solutions provide monetization opportunities for OEMs, carriers, and application ("app" or "apps") publishers and developers.
The Company reports its results of operations through the following two segments, each of which represents an operating and a reportable segment, as follows:

The Company's On Device Solutions ("ODS") business consists of products and services that simplify the discovery and delivery of mobile apps and content media for device end users. ODS is comprised of the following product and service groups:

•Application Media represents the portion of the ODS business platform that delivers apps to end users through partnerships with wireless carriers and OEMs. Application Media optimizes revenue by using proprietary technology to streamline, track, and manage app install demand from hundreds of application developers across various publishers, carriers, OEMs, and devices.

•Content Media represents the portion of the ODS business platform that presents news, weather, sports, and other content directly within the native device experience (e.g., as the start page in the mobile browser, a widget, on unlock, etc.) through partnerships with wireless carriers and OEMs. Content Media optimizes revenue by a combination of:
•Programmatic Ad Partner Revenue - advertising within the content media that's sold on an ad exchange at a market rate (cost-per-thousand ("CPM"));
•Sponsored Content - sponsored content media from third-party content providers, presented similarly to an ad, which is monetized when a recommended story is viewed (cost-per-click ("CPC")); and
•Editorial Content - owned or licensed media, presented similarly to an ad, which is monetized when the media is clicked on (CPC).

•User acquisition tools including SingleTap® and the Company's DSP ("DT DSP") that removes friction in the app install process, delivering apps to devices with a single touch, resulting in higher conversion rates.
The Company's App Growth Platform ("AGP") business consists of Advertising Solutions and Ad Monetization Solutions.
•Advertising Solutions serve two key segments: (1) App Developers and (2) Brands and Agencies - enabling them to execute targeted mobile campaigns on the Company's direct mobile app inventory.

•App Developers and other performance-focused advertisers execute mobile user acquisition campaigns for their apps and products on the Company's direct mobile app inventory. This advertiser segment utilizes products such as the DT Demand Side Platform ("DSP") and Offer Wall ("DT Offer Wall") to configure targeting, bid prices, and creative assets used for executing the campaign.

•Brands and Agencies run mobile brand-awareness campaigns on the Company's direct mobile app inventory. The advertiser segment utilizes the Company's programmatic real-time bidding technology and creative studio to build highly engaging video content that is then used exclusively in campaigns targeting the Company's direct mobile app inventory.

•Ad Monetization solutions allow mobile app publishers and developers to monetize their monthly active users via display, native, and video advertising. Our Ad Monetization solutions are integrated directly with leading mobile apps and games, connecting their ad inventory to campaigns from DSP, app marketers, brand advertisers, and agencies, primarily through a programmatic, real-time bidding auction, and, in some cases, through the Company's direct campaign management products such as the DT DSP and DT Offer Wall.

headings: We may not achieve the expected benefits of our transformation program and similar measures we take in the future, and our efforts may adversely affect our business.
We have a history of net losses, may incur substantial net losses in the future, and may not achieve or sustain profitability in the future.
We have a limited operating history for our current portfolio of assets, which may make it difficult to evaluate our business.
Our operations are global in scope, and we face added business, political, regulatory, legal, operational,
financial, and economic risks as a result of our international operations and distribution, any of which could increase our costs, hinder our operations, and return to growth.
Our financial results could vary significantly from period-to-period and are difficult to predict.
The development and use of AI in our business, combined with an uncertain regulatory environment, may adversely affect our business, reputation, financial condition, or results of operations.
Our products, services, and systems rely on software that is highly technical, and if it contains errors or viruses, our business could be adversely affected.
Our business and reputation are impacted by information technology system failures and network disruptions.
Our business may suffer if we are unable to hire and retain key talent who are in high demand.
Entry into new lines of business, and our offering of new products and services, resulting from our investments may result in exposure to new risks.
Risks Related to the Mobile Advertising Industry
The mobile advertising business is an intensely competitive industry, and we may not be able to compete successfully.
Our business is dependent on the continued growth in usage of smartphones, tablets, and other mobile connected devices.
Wireless communication technologies are changing rapidly, and we may not be successful in working with these new technologies.
The complexity of and incompatibilities among mobile devices may require us to use additional resources for the development of our products and services.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, together with all of the other information in this Annual Report, including the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," and our consolidated financial statements and the related notes, included elsewhere in this Annual Report. Our business, financial condition, results of operations, or prospects could also be adversely affected by risks and uncertainties that are not presently known to us or that we currently believe are not material. If any of the risks actually occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations, and prospects could be adversely affected. In that event, the market price of our common stock could decline, and you could lose all or part of your investment. See the summary of our risk factors under the section titled "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" under Part I of this Annual Report.

In October 2024, the Company began a transformation program intended to improve current and future operating expenses, cash flows, and personnel costs. Additionally, the initiatives intended to simplify and streamline business operations, including product optimization, procurement and cost optimization, and team restructuring. As part of the transformation program, we implemented a two-phased reduction in our workforce, one in November 2024 and the other in January 2025. The transformation program included several other initiatives and was completed in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.

The transformation program and reduction in force may yield unintended consequences and costs, such as attrition beyond our intended reduction in force, a negative effect on employee morale and productivity or our ability to attract highly skilled employees. We may further discover that, despite the savings realized from our transformation program and reduction in force, we may require additional capital to continue expanding our business, and we may be unable to obtain such capital on acceptable terms, if at all. The failure to realize the expected benefits of the completed transformation program due to the emergence of unintended consequences could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

If our transformation program does not improve operating expenses, cash flows, and personnel costs as expected or there are other unexpected operating cost increases, we may continue to incur operating net losses. If our revenue does not increase sufficiently to offset our operating expenses, we will incur losses and may not be able to achieve profitability in the future. If there are delays in the distribution of our products or if we are unable to successfully negotiate with advertisers, application developers, carriers, mobile operators, or OEMs, or if these negotiations cannot occur on a timely basis, we may not be able to generate revenue sufficient to meet the needs of the business.

The ability to evaluate our business and prospects is hindered by our limited operating history as a combined business following our acquisitions of Appreciate on March 2, 2021, AdColony on April 29, 2021, and Fyber N.V. on May 25, 2021. This challenge is further compounded by the completion of our transformation program and reduction in force as well as the risks and uncertainties in the emerging mobile application advertising industry. paragraphs: On August 29, 2025 (the "Closing Date"), the Company refinanced its existing senior credit facility. The Company and certain wholly owned subsidiaries of the Company, as guarantors (the "Guarantors"), entered into a Financing Agreement (the "Financing Agreement") with Blue Torch Finance LLC, as both administrative and collateral agent. The Financing Agreement (i) has a four-year term from the Closing Date and (ii) provides for three separate tranches of term loans in an aggregate principal amount of $430,000 (collectively the "Loans"), all of which were borrowed in full by the Company on the Closing Date. The Loans are secured by substantially all of the assets of the Company and the Guarantors, subject to certain exceptions. During the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, the Company repaid one of the three term loan tranches. See Note 12—Debt in the notes to the consolidated financial statements included in Item 8 of Part II of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information regarding the Financing Agreement.

In connection with the Financing Agreement, the Company issued warrants (the "2025 Warrants") to purchase an aggregate of 824,421 shares of the Company's common stock (the "Common Stock"), par value $0.0001 per share, to certain affiliates of the Financing Agreement's lenders at an exercise price of $4.84 per share (the "Exercise Price"), which was equal to the 30-day volume-weighted average price per share of Common Stock ending on and including the trading day immediately preceding the Closing Date. On September 15, 2025, the Company issued an additional warrant to purchase an aggregate of 397,997 shares of Common Stock to an affiliate of a lender at the Exercise Price. The warrants expire on March 1, 2030. See Note 12—Debt in the notes to the consolidated financial statements included in Item 8 of Part II of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information regarding the warrants issued in connection with the Financing Agreement.

On April 20, 2026, the Company amended its Financing Agreement and reduced the liquidity covenant requirement for the period between April 1, 2026 and December 31, 2026 from $20,000 to $15,000 and modified the timing and potential amount of certain associated fees. On April 20, 2026 the Company amended the 2025 Warrant agreement to suspend the Company's obligation to provide certain registration rights with respect to the resale of shares of Common Stock underlying the warrants held by or issuable to the holders from time to time until October 1, 2026. See Note 18—Subsequent Events in the notes to the consolidated financial statements included in Item 8 of Part II of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information regarding the amendment to the Financing Agreement.

On August 5, 2025, the Company entered into a Sale Agreement ("ATM") with RBC Capital Markets LLC and Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC as sales agents (collectively, the "Agents"), pursuant to which we could offer and sell from time-to-time shares of our Common Stock for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $150,000. During the year ended March 31, 2026, the Company sold 9,945,136 shares of Common Stock at an average selling price of $5.89 per share, yielding aggregate gross proceeds of $58,566, and incurred commission costs of $1,757 associated with such sales. Net proceeds raised under the ATM were used to prepay the principal of the Loans, as required under the Financing Agreement. On February 2, 2026, the Company delivered notice to the Agents of the termination of the ATM offering agreement.

paragraphs: Digital Turbine, Inc., 透過其子公司（合稱 "Digital Turbine," "本公司," "我們," 或 "我們"），為一領導的獨立行動裝置成長平台，提升廣告商、發行商、電信業者及裝置原廠製造商（"OEMs"）的產業生態。本公司提供端到端的產品與解決方案，運用專有技術，服務行動應用生態系的所有參與者，協助品牌發現與廣告、用戶取得與參與，以及廣告商的運營效率。此外，我們的產品與解決方案亦為 OEMs、電信業者及應用程式（"app" 或 "apps"）發行商與開發者提供 monetization 的機會。
本公司依下列兩大分部報告其營運成果，每一分部均為一營運及應報告分部，如下：
本公司 On Device Solutions（"ODS"）業務包含簡化行動應用程式與內容媒體對裝置終端用戶的發現與交付的產品與服務。ODS 由下列產品與服務組成：
•Application Media 代表 ODS 服務平台中，透過與無線電信業者及 OEMs 的合作夥伴關係，將應用程式交付終端用戶的部分。Application Media 透過專有技術，優化收入，以簡化、追蹤及管理來自數百個應用程式開發者的應用程式安裝需求，透過各類發行商、電信業者、OEMs 及裝置。
•Content Media 代表 ODS 服務平台中，直接在裝置原生體驗中呈現新聞、天氣、體育及其他內容的部分（例如：行動瀏覽器的首頁、小工具、解鎖時等），透過與無線電信業者及 OEMs 的合作夥伴關係。Content Media 透過以下方式優化收入：
•Programmatic Ad Partner Revenue - 在內容媒體中進行的廣告，於廣告交易平台以市場價格（每千次展示（"CPM"））銷售；
•Sponsored Content - 來自第三方內容供應商的贊助內容媒體，以類似廣告形式呈現，當推薦故事被觀看時進行 monetization（每點擊成本（"CPC"））；以及
•Editorial Content - 自有或授權的媒體，以類似廣告形式呈現，當媒體被點擊時進行 monetization（CPC）。
•用戶取得工具包括 SingleTap® 以及本公司之 DSP ("DT DSP")，可減少應用程式安裝流程中的摩擦，以單一觸碰方式將應用程式傳送至裝置，進而提高轉換率。
本公司之 App Growth Platform ("AGP") 事業包括廣告解決方案與廣告 monetization 解決方案。
•廣告解決方案服務兩個關鍵市場：(1) 應用程式開發者與 (2) 品牌與代理商 - 使其能在本公司之直接行動應用程式存貨上執行針對性行動行銷活動。
•應用程式開發者及其他以成效為導向的廣告主，於本公司之直接行動應用程式存貨上執行其應用程式與產品之行動用戶取得行銷活動。此廣告主市場使用 DT Demand Side Platform ("DSP") 與 Offer Wall ("DT Offer Wall") 等產品，用以設定目標對象、競標價格與用以執行行銷活動的創意資產。
•品牌與代理商於本公司之直接行動應用程式存貨上執行行動品牌認知行銷活動。此廣告主市場使用本公司之程序化即時競標技術與創意工作室，以建立高度吸引人的影片內容，並專門用於針對本公司之直接行動應用程式存貨的行銷活動。

•廣告 monetization 解決方案允許行動應用程式發行者與開發者透過顯示、原生與影片廣告，使其每月活躍用戶實現收益。本公司之廣告 monetization 解決方案直接整合至領先的行動應用程式與遊戲中，將其廣告存貨連結至 DSP、應用程式行銷者、品牌廣告主與代理商的行銷活動，主要透過程序化即時競標拍賣，並在某些情況下透過本公司之直接行銷活動管理產品，如 DT DSP 與 DT Offer Wall。

paragraphs: 於 2025 年 8 月 29 日（「結清日」），本公司重組其現有之高階信用融資協議。本公司與若干 wholly owned subsidiaries 作為擔保人（「擔保人」），與 Blue Torch Finance LLC 簽訂融資協議（「融資協議」），Blue Torch Finance LLC 同時擔任行政及擔保代理人。融資協議（i）自結清日起有四年期限，（ii）提供三筆分離之定期貸款，總本金為 430,000 美元（合稱「貸款」），本公司於結清日已全部取得貸款。貸款以本公司及擔保人 substantially all 之資產為擔保，但有若干例外。於 2026 年 3 月 31 日財務年度內，本公司已償還其中一筆定期貸款之貸款組別。有關融資協議之更多資訊，請參見本年度報告 10-K 表單第 8 項 Part II 之財務報表附註第 12 項「債務」。

配合融資協議，本公司發行認購權證（「2025 年權證」），允許購買本公司普通股（「普通股」）共 824,421 股，每股票面價值為 0.0001 美元，發給若干與融資協議貸款人有關聯之機構，認購價格為每股 4.84 美元（「認購價格」），與結清日前一個交易日之 30 日成交量加權平均價格相同。於 2025 年 9 月 15 日，本公司再發行一筆權證，允許購買普通股共 397,997 股，認購價格為每股 4.84 美元。權證於 2030 年 3 月 1 日到期。有關與融資協議相關之權證之更多資訊，請參見本年度報告 10-K 表單第 8 項 Part II 之財務報表附註第 12 項「債務」。

於 2026 年 4 月 20 日，本公司修改其融資協議，將 2026 年 4 月 1 日至 2026 年 12 月 31 日之流動性契約要求由 20,000 美元減至 15,000 美元，並修改相關費用之時間及潛在金額。於 2026 年 4 月 20 日，本公司修改 2025 年權證協議，暫停本公司提供有關普通股 resale 權利之義務，至 2026 年 10 月 1 日為止。有關修改融資協議之更多資訊，請參見本年度報告 10-K 表單第 8 項 Part II 之財務報表附註第 18 項「後續事件」。

於 2025 年 8 月 5 日，本公司與 RBC Capital Markets LLC 及 Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC 簽訂銷售協議（「ATM」），作為銷售代理人（合稱「代理人」），本公司可不時發售普通股，總共可籌得最高 150,000 美元之淨銷售額。於 2026 年 3 月 31 日財務年度內，本公司出售普通股共 9,945,136 股，平均售價為每股 5.89 美元，總共籌得淨銷售額為 58,566 美元，並產生佣金費用為 1,757 美元。ATM 之下所籌得之淨資金用以償還貸款本金，如融資協議所要求。於 2026 年 2 月 2 日，本公司通知代理人終止 ATM 發售協議。

headings: 與本公司業務相關的風險
本公司可能無法實現轉型計畫及未來所採取類似措施預期的效益，且本公司努力可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
本公司有淨虧損的歷史，未來可能產生重大淨虧損，且未來可能無法實現或維持盈利。
本公司目前資產組合的經營歷史有限，這可能使評估本公司業務變得困難。
本公司營運範圍為全球性，因國際營運及銷售業務，我們面臨額外的商業、政治、法規、法律、作業、財務及經濟風險，任何風險都可能提高我們的成本、阻礙我們的營運，並影響成長。
我們的國際營運及銷售業務，使我們面臨額外的商業、政治、法規、法律、作業、財務及經濟風險，任何風險都可能提高我們的成本、阻礙我們的營運，並影響成長。
本公司之財務表現可能於不同期間有顯著變動，且難以預測。
本公司於業務中發展與應用人工智能技術，加上不確定之監管環境，可能對本公司之業務、聲譽、財務狀況或營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司產品、服務及系統依賴高度技術性的軟體，若軟體包含錯誤或病毒，將可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司業務及聲譽可能受資訊科技系統故障及網路中斷的影響。
若本公司無法聘僱並留住高需求的關鍵人才，將可能影響本公司業務。
進入新業務領域，以及因投資而提供的新產品與服務，可能導致面臨新的風險。
訴訟可能對本公司業務造成損害。
與行動廣告產業相關的風險
行動廣告產業為一高度競爭的產業，本公司可能無法成功競爭。
本公司業務依賴智慧型手機、平板電腦及其他行動連線裝置使用量的持續成長。
無線通訊技術正在快速變更，本公司可能無法成功與這些新技術合作。
行動裝置的複雜性及相容性問題，可能需要本公司投入更多資源用於產品與服務的開發。
paragraphs: 您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並配合本年度報告中所有其他資訊，包括標題為「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」的章節，以及我們的合併財務報表與相關附註，這些資訊均包含於本年度報告其他部分。我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果或前景，也可能因目前未知或我們認為不具重大影響的風險與不確定性而受到不利影響。若任何風險實際發生，我們的業務、財務狀況、營運成果與前景可能受到不利影響。在此情況下，本公司普通股的市場價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。請參閱本年度報告第一部分標題為「對未來展望陳述之警示」的章節中，我們風險因素的總結。
2024年10月，本公司開始了一項轉型計畫，旨在改善目前與未來的營運費用、現金流與人力成本。此外，該計畫包含簡化與優化業務運作的各項措施，包括產品優化、採購與成本優化，以及團隊重整。作為轉型計畫的一部分，我們實施了兩階段的員工裁減，一階段於2024年11月，另一階段於2025年1月。轉型計畫包含多項其他措施，並於2025財年第四季完成。
轉型計畫與員工裁減可能導致未預見的後果與成本，例如超出預期裁減範圍的人員流失、員工士氣與生產力的負面影響，或我們吸引高技能員工的能力受損。我們可能進一步發現，儘管透過轉型計畫與員工裁減實現了節省，我們仍可能需要額外資金以持續擴張業務，且我們可能無法在可接受的條件下取得此資金，甚至可能無法取得。若因未預見的後果而無法實現轉型計畫預期的效益，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成重大不利影響。
若我們的轉型計畫未能如預期改善營運費用、現金流與人力成本，或出現其他未預見的營運費用增加，我們可能持續產生營運淨虧損。若我們的營收無法足夠抵銷營運費用，我們將產生虧損，且未來可能無法實現盈利。若產品發佈出現延遲，或我們無法成功與廣告主、應用開發者、電信業者、行動運營商或OEM協商，或這些協商無法在合適時間內進行，我們可能無法產生足夠的營收以支應業務需求。
評估我們的業務與前景的能力受到我們作為合併後企業的有限營運歷史所限制，此限制發生在我們於2021年3月收購Appreciate、2021年4月收購AdColony，以及2021年5月收購Fyber N.V.之後。此挑戰進一步因轉型計畫與員工裁減的完成，以及新興行動應用廣告產業的風險與不確定性而更加嚴重。為持續擴張業務，我們必須做到以下事項：
•維持現有，並發展新的，無線電信業者、OEM、應用開發者、廣告主與市場場地交換的關係，於國際與國內市場皆然；
